PE NKETII WESLEYAN MUTUAL IMPROVEMENT ASSOCIATION --The sixth session of this society was opened on Wednesday evening, in the lately en- larged Wesleyan Day School, by the inaugural ad- dress from the president,. Mr. James Watson, who took " Character " as the subject of his remarks. After touching upon the characteristics of the different nations, the president went on to discuss individual character in its various phases, and in its dinect influence on others. The address was listened to with interest and attention, and was followed by speaking from the following members: —Messrs. C. E. Parker, R. Garnett, J. Peers, D. Dobson, Dignum, and Mrs. Garnett. There was a good attendance. W YCLIFFE DEBATING SOCIETY. This society held its inaugural meeting for the coming session on Tuesday evening, when upwards of 130 persons sat down to an excellent tea,, which was very taste- fully laid out in Wycliffe Hall. After tea an ad- journment was made to the large lecture room up- stairs, when a very interesting entertainment was given, presided over by the Rev. J. Yonge. During the evening a charade was very creditably per- formed by several ladies and gentlemen in connec- tion with the society, the stage for the performance being very prettily decorated. A capital list of subjects has been made up for discussion at the weekly meetings, and altogether the society's pros- pects are very encouraging. DEATH OF Mn. Ricire_nn EVA NS. —The eldest son of the late Mr. Richard Evans, of Haydock Grange, bearing the same name as his father, the founder of the well-known firm of Lancashire colliery proprie- tors, died on Sunday at Coombe Pyne, Branksome Park, Bournemouth. Mr. Evans was in the 77th year of his age, and it is now some time since he re- I moved because of the state of his health to the more cc.ngenial atmosphere of Bournemouth. The only other survivors of the founder of the firm are Mr. Joseph Evans, J.P., of Hurst House, near Prescot, and his sister, both of whom are just now staying at Llanrwst. The deceased gentleman, we believe, like his brother, Mr. Joseph Evans, was a Liberal in politics, but never at any period of his long life took a very active part in politics, though he was more than once solicited to seek parliamen- tary honours. THE FATAL ACCIDENT TO A LABOURER.— Mr. S. Brighouse, County coroner, on Monday 'morning opened an enquiry at the Workhouse into the cause of the death of Thomas Loftus, (60) a farm labourer who died at the Workhouse, on the Friday afternoon previous from lock-jaw, under circumstances re- ported in our last issue. Mr. Birtles was foreman of the jury and Inspector Spinks was present on behalf of the police. Evidence was given to the effect that the deceased had been working for Mr. Clarke, of Seven Oaks, Great Budworth, and that on Wednesday, the 21st ult., he was in charge of a thrashing machine. The ma- chine after work was finished, was being taken to a smithy for repairs, when deceased at- tempted to jump on it while it was in motion. He failed, however, and was knocked down by the wheel of the machine, which cut his left hand in two and injured his left leg. His injuries were sub- sequently dressed at the Warrington Infirmary, whence'he was soon afterwards removed to the Workhouse Hospital, where he was attended by Dr. Spinks until the time of his death, which resulted from lock-jaw. Before his death Loftus made two statements, which were read by Inspector Spinks, and it was then suggested by the Coroner that the inquiry should be adjourned, in order that further evidence as to the accident might be obtained. In Ithis suggestion the jury concurred, and the inquiry was adjourned until Monday next with that ob- jects
pianist. The proceedings terminated with the usual votes of thanks.
FRODSHAM.

Ciruncrt LrecTruz.—A lecture on "The Church of Eng- land and Transubetentiation " was delivered in the Town Hall, Frodebam, on Tuesday evening, by Mr. George Cull- wick, of Manchever. There was a very' large attendance, and the chair WAS taken by Mr. Foulkes, FRODSHASS AND ThetSRY DRAINAOR BOARD —At the first meeting of the above Board, held in the Boardroom, Frodsham, on Tharsrlay afternoon, Mr. Henry Beswick„ of Barrow Hall, was appointed chairman of the Board for the ensuing year and the following were appointed as meFri- here of the Finance and General Purposes Committee : Messrs. H. Beswick, Thomas Davies, John Priestner, Ralph Bate, John Caton, James Percival, and Jos. Ellams. -

FOREIGN Mrasiosra —Oa Sunday morning and evening sermons were preached in the Trinity Wesleyan Chapel, Frodsbam, by the Rear.*Arthttr Shipham, from Ceylon, in aid of the Foreign Missionary Society, and on Monday evening a most successful public meeting was held in the chapel. The chair Wa9 taken by Mr. W. P. Christian, of Liverpool. Addresses having been given by the Chairman and Rev. John Shipham, the annual report was read by Mr. W. Robinson. The Rev. A. Shipharn then gave a very in- teresting address with reference to missionary work in South Ceylon, where he had laboured daring the past twelve years. The collections received at the three services amounted to £2l. being an increase of £l2 95 as compared with those of last year.
SERIOUS SMUGGLING CASH AT EUNCORN.

Atinncorn Pe-t-t; -S-es-si-(;;;;, on Monday. before—dtain Holehurat and Mr James Handley, William Ellis, master of the vessel Actlian, of Penzance, was charged with hav- ing smuggled 17Iba of manufactured tobacco, and 41bs. of cigars, the treble value and duty of which amounted to £25 lie 6d.—Mr Mitchell, supervisor of customs at Runcorn, prosecuted, and Mr A Linaker defended.—The circum- stances as shown by evidence were to this effee. Whilst the Acadian was on a voyage from Swansea to Dieppe the defendant had a conversation with a seaman named James Milburn, and other members of his crew, in which he said they could get some tobacco and take it ashore in Mounts Bay. At. Dieppe the captain obtained 221135. of tobacco (English weight) and four boxes of cigars. He also pur- chased some spirits. Milmrn purchased 51bs. of tobacco and a box of cigars from the captain, and another sailor named Jahn Hook did likewise. Mounts Bay was reached about midnight on the 15th September, and Milburn took his and his comrade's share of tobacco and oigars to the captain, who placed them in a bag. There wculd he 16 or 17 lbs. of tobacco in the bag, and a quantity of cigars. The bag was placed into a small beat, into which embarked the captain, the mate, and the mate's wife, and Milburn rowed them to the shore, where the goods were landed. The men returned to the vessel, which bad been brought to two miles from the shore, and the side lights extinguished so that the vessel could not be seen. It was arranged that the men should have their tobacco when they had completed theirjourney to Weston Point and hack to Penzance. At Weston Point, however, Milburn and the captain had a quarrel, and the former threatened to reveal the whole transaction. The captain's reply to the threat was .ed that he had telegraphed to hi 3 wife to get the tobacco out of the house. Mr.R. Lea, post-master, Runcorn, appear in the witness box, with the telegram, but he said his in. structlons were flatto produce it without the content of the sender. DINNBIL.—On Saturday 30 meilibefs of die reitrit- head and Marquis of Granby Quolnieg Clubs sat down to a dinner at the house of Mr. Joseph Roberts, the Farmer's Arms, Fearnhead, After the removal of the cloth, the evening was spern in sing- ing, &e.„ and all appeared to enjoy themselves thoroughly.

THE-Wits-a FnearammAxs.—Special services were held on Saturday and Sunday last in connec- tion with the Welsh Presbyterians, worshipping in Bold-street. On Saturday night, a service was held in the preaching room, when Mr. J. Puleston Jones, of Baliol College, Oxford,. a blind preacher, gave an excellent sermon to a large congregation. On S today afternoon and evening the services were- held in the Public Hall, and were' largely attended. Mr. 3. P. Jones preaChed on eacit omission, and the collections, which were in aid Of the church funds, realised the sum of .£9 10s. Sr. PAUL'S HARVEST THANKSGIVING SERVICES. The annual harvest thanksgiving services 4 were commenced in it. Paul's Church, on Thursday even- ing. The sacred edifice had been most attractively decorated for the occasion by a number of the laxly ' members of the- church, and there was a large and attentive congregation. The preacher was the Rev. Canon Rycroft ; the ssons being read by the Rev. G. Wray (St..Petera). and the Rev. G. Smithh The Vicar, the Rev.. S. Wilkinson, read the prayers. The other clergymen present were the Rev. IC ,Phillips (curate), and the Rev. I. Phillips (Orford.) The collections were in aid of the church funds. The services will be continued to-morrow (Sunday). lIIESEbITATION.—On Saturday evening, in Silver- street Schoolroom, an interesting presentation was made to Mr. James Horton (eldest son of Mr. W. J. Horton of Lorne Villa, Froghall-lane), who has !accepted. 'an appointment at Valparaiso, Chili. The presents- consisted of at handsomely-bound Spanish Bible and dictionary.. After an excellent tea, to which about 50 persons sat down, which was pro- vided by Mr. and Mrs-Dallow, Mr. J. Shaw Green was elected chairman, and an entertainment, con- sisting: of songs, rendered by Miss L. Horton, Mr. James Hbrton, Mr. Dallove, Mr. Tatton (Manchester), andthe members of the-choir, was gone through. Speeches were made by the Chairman, Mr. Howell, Mr. John Houghton, Mr. Dallow, and Sergeant-Major Tudball, :who expressed their regret that Mr. Hor- ton was-about to leave them, and wished him suc- cess and happiness in his new sphere of labour. Mr. Horton suitably responded: BANK "QUAY BOWLING GREEN.—A considerable number of interested spectators gathered at the Bank Quay Subscription Bowling Green, on Satur-. day afternoon, when a handicap mint promoted by Mr. Robert Mellor, the landlord of the Bowling , Green Hotel, for the employees of Messrs. J. Cros- field and Sons, took place. Nearly 30 competitors entered the lists, and the green being in splendid condition some exciting play was witnessed. The first prize, a valuable pair of bowls, presented by Mr. Mellor, with ss, was won by John Bandies; 2nd, George Slider; 3rd. Sam Welsby ; and 4th George Wilcock. Several other minor prizes were also awarded. On Thursday afternoon a match was played between Mr. William Bi,llian (president), and Mr. Joseph Massey (treasurer), who were opposed by Messrs Edward Macauley awl , William Gleave, two members of the committee. The first-named couple won by one point, the score being 21 up. The players and a number of friends subsequently par- took of an enjoyable supper and spent the evening in a social manner. THE REMOVAL OF THE PARISH CHURCH CURATE: MEETING OF PARISHIONERThe somewhat unex- pecte I removal of the Rev. Mi.. Twist, curate of the Parish Church has caused a feeling of regket among the parishioners, by whom he was highly respected. During his stay in the parish for the .past nine months, Mr. Twist was especially active in his min- isterial duties, the poor people being regularly visited, while his zeal and energy were manifested in every form of parochial labour. It is stated that M. '..: ist has been removed by the Lord Bishop: of the Diocese, but upon what ground has not been publicly stated. A meeting Of the parishioners to consider the question was held in the Parish Church Boys' School, Church-street, on Thurs- day evening, when there was a g6od at- tendance. Mf. N. B. Percival, senior church- warden, occupied the chair, and among the gentle- men present were Messrs, L.W. Francomb, .T. E. Wright, W. Brooks, John Dewhurst, J. P. Leigh, John Gaskell. F. Taylor, Isherwood, Greenway, Burgess. Sergeant Price, and others. The feeling of regret at the loss sustained by the Rev. Mr. Twist's removal was unanimously expressed, and a petition, to the Lord Bishop, praying him to allow the rev. gentleman named to remain in the parisji was unanimously adopted. The petition had bead signed by about 500 parishioners; . and a further motion was passed that the two churchwardens should be appointed a deputation to present the petition to the Bishop.

John Rylands (chairman), Darby- shire, Blackhurst, Greening, Long, Ratcliffe, Bal- harry ; S. Sutton (assistant clerk), and a number of assistant overseers.—Mr. Owen reported the follow- ing valuations made in accordance with instruc- tions:—Mr. William Mortimer, Orford tannery, ad- ditions, gross £2B 10s,.rateable £24; Messrs. P. Walker and Sons, Dallam Brewery, additions, gross £l3B 10,, rateable £111; Messrs. Joseph Crosfleld and Sons, Bank Quay Soapery, additions. gross .£l2O, rateable £9O; Messrs. T. Fletcher and Co., Thynne- street, additions, gross £7B loq, rateable £O6; Messrs. J. Blundell and Sons, coal-yard, Dannet- street, gross £7O, rateable £6O. In consequence of the portion of the premises of Mr. Samuel Horton having been let off to Messrs. Blundell. and assessed as above, the assessment of these works would be reduced to gross £lO3. rateable DO. Messrs. Ware- ing and Co., Buckley-street: On Saturday, the Ist of October, he visited these works and went over the whole, as instructed at the last meeting. All work was suspended on the 29th September, and there was now no work of any kind being carried on there. There was still some unsold stock warehoused on the premises, and he was of opinion that a tem- porary assessment of gross £2O, rateable £l7, would cover this use of the, premises together with the warehousing of the•engine. The report was adopted.—A brief discussion took place with regard to the rating of elementary schools in the Union, and it was decided, on the motion of Mr. Darbyshire, seconded by Mr. Long, that the suggestion 'made by the Valuer at the previous meeting,that these schools be assessed at the rate of .£2 far every 100 scholars accommo- dated, was adopted.—Several appeal cases of an ordinary character were dealt with. GREAT SANLRY' SCHOOL BOARD.—The monthly meeting of this Board was held at the schools, Great Sankey, on Thursday afternoon. There were present Mr. Ridgway (chairman), the Rev. E. S. Jackson, Messrs. Skelton, Hatton, Grange, and S. Sutton (clerk.)—The Clerk submitted a statement of ac- counts for the year ended 29th September, 1887, from which it appeared that the total receipts, in- cluding a balance at the beginning of the year of £4Ol Os 7d, were £797 15s 4d. The expendi- ture had been £743 /6s sd, a balance being left ot £53 18s lid in the hands of the treasurer. Of the above amount £253 15s 2d had been paid out of loan, thus leaving a net expenditure of the Board of £490 Is 3d for the year. The estimate of income and expenditure for the coming year was also sub-, mitted. For ineome it showed as follows :—Balance in treasurer's hands. £53 18s 11d, probable grant from Government (17 months) £250; school fees, , £150; sale of books and materials, £5; total, £458 18s 11d. The total estimated expenditure was £551, which, after allowing for estimated income of £458 18s 11d, left £92 is id to be raised by the rates. It was accordingly resolved that the over- seers be required to pay the sum of £92 in respect of the expenditure of the coming year. The Clerk , explained that this amount would mean a rate of 3d in the .£ for the year, and the Chairman, the Rev. E. S. Jackson, and other members expressed them- selves pleased that the rate would be so low, and hoped it would be maintained at the same figure.— An application for increase of wages from Mrs. Rigby, school cleaner, was considered, and it was agreed that her pay should be raised from 6s per week to 7s 6d.—The Clerk read an announcement from the Education Department that Mr. Syder, her Mayesty's inspector of schools, would visit the Board Schools on Friday, October 14th, for the pur- pose of making the annual examination and in- , spection.—This was all the business of public in- terest. div.head: ALLEGED MANSLAUGHTER AT STOCKTON HEATH.
div.p: ALLEGED MANSLAUGHTER AT STOCKTON HEATH.

On Monday an inquest was held by Mr. Wore coroner, at the Mulberry Tree Inn, Stockton Heath,. relative to the death from injuries to his head ef Joseph William Newton. It seemed from the evi- dence that on the 10th July there had been some disturbance and two men, named Hart, went to the house of Newton, who was their brother-in-law. It was stated that while Newton was putting one of the Harts out of his house he fell and caused an in- jury to his head. For some days after Newton did not seek medical advice with regard to the wound, but on the sth August Dr.. Argo was called in, and that gentleman attended him till his death on the 13th September. Death, it was stated, was the re- sult of the injury to the head. Prior to his death, it appears, that Newton called in Mr. Whitley, shop- keeper, and to him made a statement, which was taken down in writing, to the effect that the injury was caused by a fall and that no one was to be blamed for it. In reply to Sergeant Booth, Mrs Newton denied that she had told him (Sergeant Booth) on the night oft-he 19th July that her hus- bind's wound was caused by falling on some broken bottles on the door of their house. She asserted that the wound was the result of the fall sustained while &Ceased was putting her brother out of the house. An open verdict was returned to the effect that deceased died from an inj.usy to his skull re- ceived on the 19th July. On Thursday, at the in- stance of the Cheshire police, John Hart, one of the men referred to as having gone to the house of the deceased, was arrested at Runcorn, and yesterday he was brought before Mr. R. Pierpoint, at the ' office in Bank-street, and charged with the man- slaughter of Joseph William Newton. The case was net, however, gone into, a remand being asked for, and granted, until Thursday next.
